transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (ZenWave Head of ML Ops), Liam O'Connor (ZenWave CTO), Mei Tan (ZenWave Infra)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
ZenWave is approaching the end of their current reserved capacity term and is interested in a 12-month contract extension combined with an APAC region add-on. Key concerns: cost per token at scale, APAC latency targets, data residency/SOC2 audit needs, and fallbacks in case of regional capacity constraints. Redwood to provide updated pricing, a benchmark plan for their 50B model in APAC, and a contract amendment.

Topics: contract extension; APAC region onboarding; capacity sizing; SLA and audit/compliance; next steps & timing

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. Diego and I will run through the plan for the extension and APAC add-on—real quick check, is now still good?
[00:00:12] Priya: Yeah, good to go. We're on a slightly tight timeline so we wanna make decisions this month.
[00:00:18] Liam: Hi, thanks—I'll jump in if we go into infra too deep.
[00:00:23] Diego: Cool. Mei, thanks for sending the peak RPS snapshot earlier, that helped a ton. I'm gonna reference it as we talk about sizing.
[00:00:32] Mei: No problem, Diego. I should say some of the numbers are spiky because of batch jobs, hope that's fine.
[00:00:40] Samira: Perfect. High level: ZenWave's reserved capacity ends in August, and you asked about 12-month extension plus adding APAC region for lower latency there—right?
[00:00:51] Priya: Yep. Our mobile-first features are growing in SEA and Australia; current latency from our APAC users is around 220–300ms to the EU region, too high. We want under 120ms p95 if possible.
[00:01:03] Liam: And we also want a pricing model that doesn't explode if usage spikes by 2x for a quarter.
[00:01:10] Samira: Totally. Two levers to consider: increase committed capacity (reserved GPUs) which lowers unit price, and add APAC pool either as dedicated reserved or as burst/backup. There's also our Smart Routing option to route by latency with fallback to EU if APAC capacity is saturated.
[00:01:27] Priya: Can you remind us the difference in cost between dedicated APAC vs enabling APAC as burst-capacity on the existing commitment?
[00:01:34] Diego: Sure—simplifying: dedicated APAC reserved pools require a region add-on commit and give you predictable throughput and lower token unit price in that region; burst APAC uses shared capacity and is cheaper upfront but can be throttled during peak times. For a target p95 under 120ms we usually recommend dedicated for production critical flows.
[00:01:51] Mei: If we do dedicated, can we pin the model version in APAC separately? We sometimes want a slightly smaller quantized variant for lower cost there.
[00:01:59] Diego: Yes, you can pin model versions per region; you can also set routing policies to prefer a quantized variant in APAC for cost while keeping a higher-fidelity variant in EU as fallback. There is a slight difference in output sometimes because of quantization but for most reranking and summarization flows it's fine.
[00:02:15] Priya: OK that's helpful. Two other things—SOC 2 renewal in Q3 and a customer data residency audit for APAC. Does Redwood support region-level audit logs and KMS key separation?
[00:02:25] Samira: Yes. For Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and region-scoped audit logs. We'll include the SOC 2 artifacts and the APAC data flow diagram in the packet I'll send.
[00:02:36] Mei: We may need an on-prem package if the auditor pushes back, but let's not assume that now.
[00:02:42] Liam: Pricing—we had a sticker from last year; can we get a blended per-token price for the whole commit that keeps spikes somewhat sheltered? Meaning a cushion so short-term surges don't kill us.
[00:02:52] Samira: We can propose a tiered commit: base reserved capacity sized for typical steady-state, plus a burst allowance and a capped overage rate. For instance, a 12-month commit with a 20% burst buffer and a capped overage fee tends to be acceptable. I'll model three options in the pricing sheet.
[00:03:06] Priya: Sounds good. What's your SLA for APAC dedicated pools?
[00:03:10] Diego: Same SLA as Dedicated elsewhere: 99.9% uptime for the serving path, latency SLOs aren't SLA-backed in the same way but we do provide latency targets and capacity guarantees for reserved pools.
[00:03:21] Priya: Noted. In the past, when we've worked with other providers, cold starts in new regions were a problem, especially for large context lengths—how do you handle KV cache warmup?
[00:03:31] Diego: We have prefix and KV cache warmup helpers—when you deploy a model variant in a new pool we can pre-warm by replaying representative prompts (we'll need that dataset or your sample prompts). Also we allocate a small warm pool for steady-state to minimize cold start latency spikes.
[00:03:47] Mei: Replaying prompts—do you need anything special? Security wise, we can't send PHI in raw form.
[00:03:53] Diego: Understood. You can send anonymized prompts or synthetic data that matches length and token distribution; that'll be enough for warmup.
[00:03:59] Priya: Good. Liam, are you comfortable with the 12-month term? We're often cautious about locking in if model needs change quickly.
[00:04:06] Liam: We're open to 12 months if there's a clear break clause tied to major infra regressions or if the contract allows a limited re-negotiation window at month 6. Not asking for a full exit, but some flexibility.
[00:04:16] Samira: We can make a half-year review clause. We do price for the committed term, but can include a review at month 6 to adjust burst allowances or routing policies.
[00:04:25] Priya: That would help. Also the legal team flagged that they want a defined disaster recovery runbook specifically for the APAC pool and cross-region failover steps.
[00:04:34] Samira: We'll include an RD/DR runbook draft and the failover policy. Our standard is automatic failover to fallback pools, with a configurable policy and manual controls.
[00:04:44] Mei: Quick technical question: our model uses KV cache heavily and sessions often exceed 4k tokens—any comp issues with offloading KV or memory pressures in APAC smaller instances?
[00:04:54] Diego: If you're running long contexts we usually recommend larger instance types in those pools to avoid frequent KV eviction; alternatively, we can enable a hybrid KV mode which spills less frequently but increases per-hour cost. We'll include instance sizing suggestions in the benchmark plan.
[00:05:08] Priya: Okay. Can you talk through the benchmark you mentioned? What's the minimum you need from us?
[00:05:14] Diego: For a useful baseline: 1) representative prompt set (anonymized) for warmup and p95 testing; 2) peak RPS profile (you already shared an initial snapshot—thanks); 3) model version and any quantized variants you plan to run. We'll run cold start, steady-state, and spike tests.
[00:05:30] Priya: We'll produce synthetic prompts for privacy.
[00:05:34] Samira: Great. On the commercial side, I'll model three commitment scenarios: 6-month extension, 12-month extension, and 12-month plus APAC dedicated. Each will show blended token price, burst buffer, and overage cap.
[00:05:47] Liam: Please call out the price delta if we switch model variants in APAC to a 4-bit quantized variant vs running full float.
[00:05:55] Samira: Will do—Diego will give rough perf deltas, I'll translate to cost estimates.
[00:06:01] Mei: Slight background noise—sorry, connection is patchy for me (interrupts).
[00:06:06] [crosstalk] Priya: No worries, Mei.
[00:06:10] Diego: Quick note—we saw Anthropic being mentioned earlier; if you run into them in procurement, our differentiator there is the unified observability and rollout controls, plus the ability to run the same config in Private deployments if you need on-prem later.
[00:06:24] Liam: Good to know. Procurement will start scoping later this month.
[00:06:29] Priya: One more procurement ask: can Redwood produce a short table comparing contract terms (notice period, penalty for early termination, data handling) versus a self-hosted option? They want to see the tradeoffs.
[00:06:39] Samira: We can produce a concise comparison doc. I'll coordinate with legal and solutions to get that out.
[00:06:46] Mei: About timelines—if we sign an amendment mid-June, how fast can APAC dedicated pools be provisioned?
[00:06:52] Diego: Typically 2–4 weeks to provision, but with pre-approved commits and a small warm pool we can target the lower end; if you need sub-2-week we'll need to prioritize capacity and may require a small acceleration fee.
[00:07:06] Priya: For a September product launch we realistically need APAC capacity by mid-August to run QA. That sounds tight but workable.
[00:07:14] Samira: Ok, timeline noted—I'll show provisioning lead times in the proposal.
[00:07:18] Liam: Any hidden costs like data egress or storage for embeddings? Make them explicit in the sheet.
[00:07:24] Samira: Will call those out. We bill tokens and embeddings separately; small storage fees for persisted embeddings; egress gets listed when crossing cloud regions—will make that explicit for APAC flows.
[00:07:36] Priya: Great. On roles: we'll want RBAC to limit who in ZenWave can issue model rollouts to production. Does Redwood support fine-grained roles?
[00:07:44] Diego: Yes, SAML/SAML2 or OIDC single sign-on, with RBAC and per-route tokens. We'll share our RBAC matrix doc.
[00:07:53] [00:09:01] Speaker 1: (auto-label glitch) Quick check—who owns the SOC2 artifacts?
[00:09:06] Samira: Redwood will provide SOC2 reports and you can pull audit logs for compliance. I'll include the SOC2 bundle.
[00:09:12] Priya: Thanks.
[00:09:15] Diego: Back to the benchmark plan—I'll propose a 48-hour run in APAC: one cold-builder day then steady-state 24 hours with two spike windows. That should highlight cold start behavior and peak cost.
[00:09:28] Mei: Perfect.
[00:09:31] Samira: Next steps—I'll send the pricing scenarios, the contract amendment draft, SOC2 + compliance artifacts, and an RD/DR runbook. Diego will share the benchmark plan and the list of sample inputs we need.
[00:09:44] Priya: We'll anonymize and send prompts by Friday.
[00:09:48] Liam: Procurement will want the comparison doc.
[00:09:51] Samira: Understood. We'll aim to get everything in a single packet early next week.
[00:09:56] [00:10:03] Diego: Any other technical risks we should call out now?
[00:10:07] Priya: Nothing else from my side.
[00:10:09] Mei: Same.
[00:10:11] Liam: No.
[00:10:14] Samira: Great—recap quickly: 1) Samira to send pricing options and contract amendment draft; 2) Diego to run and share APAC benchmark plan; 3) ZenWave to supply anonymized prompts and infra peak RPS diagram; 4) follow-up meeting week of 2026-06-22 to finalize.
[00:10:32] Priya: That matches our expectations.
[00:10:35] Liam: Thanks everyone.
[00:10:38] Samira: Thanks all—we'll follow up in the thread with the packet.

(Transcript ends—auto transcription had some label errors and occasional mis-heard words like "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" and "V-P-C" for VPC.)
